summary: Verified the async import background-job fix. Backend: POST /api/import/start returns job_id in <2s (not blocking 60s), GET /api/import/jobs/{id} polls to 'done'. DOCX end-to-end extraction returned 75 questions with batch categorisation (chapter=Hydrocarbons, difficulty=hard, tags=pyq+important) correctly applied; /import/commit persisted questions. Frontend /admin/import workflow completed: parse-btn triggered the async job, review-row-0 appeared after ~55s, 75 review rows rendered, 'Detected 75 question(s) (AI-assisted)' toast displayed, Chapter: Hydrocarbons applied per question. One failure: the sample Solutions PDF (import_mode=extract with solutions auto-switch to adapt) returned count=0 with a 'Invalid \escape' JSON parse error from the AI — the async-job plumbing is fine, but the adapt-mode AI output is unparseable for this PDF.

minor.issue: Sample Hydrocarbons_Solutions.pdf completes job with status='done' but result.count=0. Errors returned: ["This PDF contains solutions, not the original questions...", "Parse error: Invalid \\escape: line 1 column 3507 (char 3506)"]. The auto-switch extract->adapt fires but the AI response contains an invalid backslash escape so JSON decoding fails and no adapted practice questions are produced. ai_parser JSON recovery does not sanitise raw backslashes before loading.

action_items: Harden ai_parser JSON recovery for adapt-mode outputs: strip/escape stray backslashes (or ask the model again) so Hydrocarbons_Solutions.pdf (and similar solution-only PDFs) actually produce the ~40 adapted practice questions instead of count=0.
Optional: when auto-switching extract->adapt and adapt also fails, bubble a user-friendlier error than 'Invalid \escape' to the UI.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py _do_import_parse auto-switch (line ~434) depends on parse_visual_pdf+AI succeeding on second pass; add a final fallback or at least surface a clearer failure (currently user sees count=0 and the raw 'Invalid \escape' line).
import_jobs collection grows unbounded — no TTL / cleanup for completed jobs; consider a TTL index or periodic sweep.
/api/import/start uses asyncio.create_task without storing a reference; if the loop GC's the task mid-run it could silently drop. Fine today but worth tracking in a background-task registry.
server.py is 3533 lines — well over the 700-line guideline; split import/exam/live-class modules into routers for maintainability.
test_credentials: admin@examnest.io / Admin@123 / role=admin (role required). Login UI uses role tabs (Student/Teacher/Parent/Admin) and 'Sign in' button, not a <select>.
seed_data_creation: test_commit_saves_questions inserted 3 questions tagged chapter=Hydrocarbons into questions collection (via /api/import/commit); safe to leave or clean up by chapter filter.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The async-job fix for the 60s gateway timeout is confirmed working for text/DOCX inputs. If retesting the PDF path after an AI parser fix, use /app/tests/sample_imports/Hydrocarbons_Solutions.pdf with subject_default=Chemistry and either import_mode=extract (will auto-switch) or import_mode=adapt; expected ~40 adapted questions. Difficulty select in the UI (cat-difficulty) is a shadcn <button role='combobox'> — Playwright page.fill will fail; use click + option. Backend assertion of difficulty applied through form field already covered by API test. Use `pytest -n 0` because /app/backend/pytest.ini pins -n 2.
rca of the issue: AI import 60s 502: Fix validated — /api/import/start returns in <2s and the async worker + /api/import/jobs/{id} polling bypasses the Emergent 60s gateway cap. DOCX extraction takes ~45-55s end-to-end and succeeds. Residual issue: for solutions-only PDFs the extract->adapt auto-switch invokes the AI again, but the AI's JSON output contains an unescaped backslash and `json.loads` raises 'Invalid \escape', producing count=0. Mitigation for next iteration: in ai_parser.ai_extract_questions, pre-sanitise the JSON string (replace `\\` not followed by a valid escape with `\\\\`, or use a regex-based fixer / json5), or add a retry prompt.
